questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country I had been to before, a culture I would fit into, a good university, and interesting subjects to study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great teachers, interesting courses, an amazing international group (ESN) that arranged trips and activities where I met many international students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest, given the fact that some of the sites on the university's website are in Italian.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the platform AirBnB.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depends on the location, but the public transportation can be unreliable and slow.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to look through the course catalogue and find courses I could take. The website was a bit confusing, but once you figure it out all the necessary information is available. Then I had to sign up for the courses, and myself apply for my schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the teachers on the courses and the international coordinator, they have been very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have questions write mails to the teachers or the international coordinator.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great level, amazing teachers and interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Perfect level, not too hard and not too easy. Challenging in terms of that it was different kinds of assessments and teaching styles than I have been used to at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More group work and active participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Digital Marketing and Innovation = 9 ECTS
- Digital Society = 9 ECTS
- Behavioural Sociology = 9 ECTS
- Introduction to R = 3 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Digital Marketing and Innovation (9 ECTS): Great teacher, relevants topics, and interesting cases. Digital Society (9 ECTS): Great teachers and relevant topics. Behavioural Sociology (9 ECTS): Great teacher and really interesting topics.

questions.answer: Foods from supermarkets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The organisation ESN was amazing. I have attended city trips to different parts of Italy and many social activities, where I met amazing people from all around the world.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: City trips, sports, museum visits, park picnics, restaurant trips, parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above. Visit different cities within Italy, it is very convenient and cheap with the train.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on city trips and social activities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me it was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the ESN events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, people are more open and talkative in Italy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmness of the Italian people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate in all the activities, be open to learn new people and explore the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt about anything, write to the teachers or the international coordinator.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything. I have grown to not find it nervewrecking to meet new people. My English has improved. I have met amazing people, and have enjoyed being surrounded my Italian people and their culture. This has been one of the best trips of my life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out the Italian transport system, and small things such as getting a travel card was very challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange, you will not regret it, you will get amazing memories for life!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
